react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites resolve to seven ChEBI-canonical compounds (warfarin sodium was excluded from all pathway hits due to its xenobiotic nature). Across three complementary paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct network enrichment — the single dominant finding is **Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism** (KEGG:hsa00140 / SMPDB:SMP00068 / MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism). This pathway ranks #1 in all three tools with FDR as low as 4.97 × 10⁻¹⁸ (RaMP), p = 5.77 × 10⁻⁷ (MetaboAnalystR), and p = 8.40 × 10⁻⁵ (Mummichog). Six driver metabolites participate: testosterone (C00535), dihydrotestosterone (C03917), androstenedione (C00280), dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), estrone (C00468), and 17β-estradiol (C00951). These six span the entire steroidogenesis axis — upstream C19-pregnenoid precursors (DHEA, androstenedione), the key C19-androgen intermediates (testosterone, DHT), and the C18-aromatised estrogens (estrone, estradiol) — indicating systemic disruption of the CYP17A1 / aromatase / 17β-HSD node. A secondary, smaller signal arises from **Tyrosine Metabolism** (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism, rank 2, p = 0.0277), driven solely by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043), a toxic aldehyde product of dopamine / norepinephrine deamination, consistent with oxidative stress or monoamine-oxidase inhibition in the treatment group. Warfarin (C01541) did not annotate to any enriched pathway, as expected for a synthetic coumarin anticoagulant. The biological story is one of broad perturbation of steroid hormone biosynthesis and catabolism, most consistent with exposure to a steroidogenic agent or CYP450 enzyme modulator.

react_result.final_narrative_json: {"narrative_text":"The eight differentially abundant metabolites resolve to a coherent steroid hormone signature. Over-representation analysis via RaMP-DB identifies 17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency as the top-ranked pathway (p < 0.05), reflecting perturbed androgen-to-estrogen interconversion. The driver metabolites androstenedione (KEGG:C00280) and testosterone (KEGG:C00535) are both elevated, consistent with impaired 17-beta-HSD III activity blocking the conversion of androstenedione to testosterone and of testosterone to 17beta-estradiol. Estradiol (KEGG:C00951) and estrone (KEGG:C00468) are also detected in the differential set, further supporting global disruption of C18/C19/C21 steroid flux. Dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227) and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917) expand the signal across the steroidogenesis axis. react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites resolve to a coherent steroid hormone signature. Over-representation analysis via RaMP-DB identifies 17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency as the top-ranked pathway (p < 0.05), reflecting perturbed androgen-to-estrogen interconversion. The driver metabolites androstenedione (KEGG:C00280) and testosterone (KEGG:C00535) are both elevated, consistent with impaired 17-beta-HSD III activity blocking the conversion of androstenedione to testosterone and of testosterone to 17beta-estradiol. Estradiol (KEGG:C00951) and estrone (KEGG:C00468) are also detected in the differential set, further supporting global disruption of C18/C19/C21 steroid flux. Dehydroepiandrosterone (KEGG:C01227) and dihydrotestosterone (KEGG:C03917) expand the signal across the steroidogenesis axis. Warfarin (KEGG:C01541) and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (KEGG:C04043) annotate to distinct metabolic modules outside the top-ranking pathway but are consistent with parallel xenobiotic and monoamine-derived aldehyde signals. The convergence of six steroid hormones on the 17-beta-HSD node constitutes the primary biological finding, with the aldehyde and anticoagulant metabolites representing secondary contextual perturbation.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites resolve to seven ChEBI-canonical compounds (warfarin sodium was excluded from all pathway hits due to its xenobiotic nature). Across three complementary paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct network enrichment — the single dominant finding is **Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism** (KEGG:hsa00140 / SMPDB:SMP00068 / MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism). This pathway ranks #1 in all three tools with FDR as low as 4.97 × 10⁻¹⁸ (RaMP), p = 5.77 × 10⁻⁷ (MetaboAnalystR), and p = 8.40 × 10⁻⁵ (Mummichog). Six driver metabolites participate: testosterone (C00535), dihydrotestosterone (C03917), androstenedione (C00280), dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), estrone (C00468), and 17β-estradiol (C00951). These six span the entire steroidogenesis axis — upstream C19-pregnenoid precursors (DHEA, androstenedione), the key C19-androgen intermediates (testosterone, DHT), and the C18-aromatised estrogens (estrone, estradiol) — indicating systemic disruption of the CYP17A1 / aromatase / 17β-HSD node. A secondary, smaller signal arises from **Tyrosine Metabolism** (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism, rank 2, p = 0.0277), driven solely by 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (C04043), a toxic aldehyde product of dopamine / norepinephrine deamination, consistent with oxidative stress or monoamine-oxidase inhibition in the treatment group. Warfarin (C01541) did not annotate to any enriched pathway, as expected for a synthetic coumarin anticoagulant. The biological story is one of broad perturbation of steroid hormone biosynthesis and catabolism, most consistent with exposure to a steroidogenic agent or CYP450 enzyme modulator.
